<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="כסלו_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518915689_theRebbe_467" batchId="meluket-_D7_9B_D7_A1_D7_9C_D7_95_meluket__BH_POST_1766518915689_theRebbe_467__p004">
  <section v="9">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that the order of Torah, charity, and prayer is from lower to higher, with prayer being superior as an elevation.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">But still, it must be said,</t>
    <t s="1">for the Torah is eternal.</t>
    <t s="2">From this it is forced that the order of these three matters in this maamar</t>
    <t s="3">is also applicable now.</t>
    <t s="4">And it can be explained according to what is explained elsewhere</t>
    <t s="5">that in elevation one can reach a higher level than in drawing down.</t>
    <t s="6">And accordingly,</t>
    <t s="7">prayer, which is an elevation from below upward,</t>
    <t s="8">its virtue is greater than that of Torah and charity.</t>
    <t s="9">And based on this, the order of these three matters will be understood even now,</t>
    <t s="10">that this order is from below upward: first—Torah,</t>
    <t s="11">then charity,</t>
    <t s="12">which</t>
    <t s="13">(now)</t>
    <t s="14">is above Torah,</t>
    <t s="15">and then prayer,</t>
    <t s="16">whose virtue is greater than the drawing down of Torah and charity,</t>
    <t s="17">as above.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="10">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section distinguishes between two aspects of Torah, charity, and communal prayer: one relating to the world and one relating to the person performing them.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">2.</t>
    <t s="1">And to understand what is said, "All who engage, etc.,"</t>
    <t s="2">which speaks about a person who engages, and not about the matters of Torah, charity, and communal prayer themselves,</t>
    <t s="3">in the engagement of Torah, charity, and communal prayer,</t>
    <t s="4">which are the general three lines,</t>
    <t s="5">there are two matters: one—what pertains to the world,</t>
    <t s="6">that in the world the matters of the three lines should be actualized,</t>
    <t s="7">so that through this there will be a dwelling place for Him, blessed be He, in the lower realms.</t>
    <t s="8">And the second—what pertains to the person who serves,</t>
    <t s="9">that he must do [his service] in these three matters.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="11">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section draws a parallel to eating holy offerings, which also has two aspects: a commandment upon the eater and a concern for the offerings themselves.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">(And analogous to what is in the eating of holy offerings, where there are two matters: one—it is a mitzvah to eat the sacrifice,</t>
    <t s="1">and this mitzvah is upon the person who eats,</t>
    <t s="2">and it has several conditions</t>
    <t s="3">(regarding anointing,</t>
    <t s="4">for greatness,</t>
    <t s="5">he is not liable).</t>
    <t s="6">The second—regarding the holy offerings themselves,</t>
    <t s="7">that they should not come to be leftover</t>
    <t s="8">(and in this matter, the conditions of anointing, etc., are not relevant).</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
